primitives.name: Waitlist Access Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: This gate implements the same hard-stop at zero cost using Next.js middleware and Basic Auth, enforced entirely server-side before the page renders.
primitives.assumptions: Middleware intercepts all requests to /waitlist paths before rendering; credentials are validated server-side only.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When GSE_WAITLIST_GATE_ENABLED ≠ true, gate is inactive and requests pass through without authentication.

layer2.mapping: The middleware-based access control mirrors traditional HTTP Basic Auth but embedded within Next.js framework for seamless integration.
layer2.telemetry: HTTP 401 responses with WWW-Authenticate header confirm denial; browser-native dialog confirms client-side interaction.

primitives.name: Cost-Free Deployment
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Cost **$0** — no Vercel add-ons, no third-party services, no subscriptions.
primitives.assumptions: No external dependencies or premium features required for access enforcement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs if Vercel Pro plan is needed for equivalent functionality.

layer2.mapping: Zero-cost deployment emerges as a derived kernel from middleware implementation avoiding Vercel’s paid protections.
layer2.telemetry: Deployment logs show no usage of Vercel Pro features; environment variables suffice for access control.

primitives.name: Authorization Header Check
primitives.verbatim_quote: If enabled, the middleware checks the `Authorization: Basic <base64>` header.
primitives.assumptions: Client sends base64-encoded credentials in standard format; server decodes and compares against stored values.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid or missing Authorization header triggers HTTP 401 response.

layer2.mapping: The check aligns with RFC 2617 Basic Authentication protocol, ensuring compatibility across clients.
layer2.telemetry: Requests with valid headers proceed; invalid ones return 401 with WWW-Authenticate directive.
